analogies: a tilted X with a long diagonal spine
two tiny flags fastened to a diagonal pole
a lightning-struck X
pick: tilted X with a diagonal spine
why: Three strokes cross at a diagonal; unlike Tav, there is no top roof.
teachingBeat: Ari traces the slanted spine, then taps its two arms.

analogies: a box with its left wall missing and a floor sticking right
a square backpack open on the left
a blocky C with a long bottom shoe
pick: open-left box with an extra-long floor
why: Flat top plus flat bottom distinguishes rounded Kaf; no inner bar unlike Pe.
teachingBeat: Noa slides a little toy car along the long bottom floor.

analogies: a walking stick with a little forward foot
a person taking a giant step
a tall coat hook with one angled leg
pick: walking stick taking a step
why: A downward slanting leg gives Gimel its step, missing from Nun or Vav.
teachingBeat: Ari says, “Spot the stepping foot!”

analogies: the top-right corner of a square table
a roof with one straight right-hand post
a squared-off upside-down L
pick: square table corner
why: The sharp corner and projecting roof separate Dalet from Resh’s rounded shoulder.
teachingBeat: Noa points to its sharp table corner.

analogies: a doorway with a loose left post
a square doorway with a gap on the left
a little house frame missing one wall section
pick: doorway with detached left post
why: Left post is visibly detached below the roof; Chet and Tav attach differently.
teachingBeat: Noa points at the daylight gap between roof and left post.

analogies: a single hanging nail
a thin wall hook with a short head
a straight pencil with a tiny top cap
pick: single hanging nail
why: One narrow shaft and short hook, with neither Zayin’s broad hat nor final Nun’s greater depth.
teachingBeat: Ari hangs one paper tag on a single nail.

analogies: a nail wearing a wide baseball cap
a tiny mushroom on a straight stem
a flat-topped thumbtack
pick: nail with a wide baseball cap
why: A distinctly wide top overhang differentiates it from thin Vav.
teachingBeat: Noa sets a wide cap above a skinny peg.

analogies: a flat bridge on two attached posts
a rectangular soccer goal without a net
a sturdy doorway with both posts connected
pick: bridge with both legs attached
why: Both verticals touch the horizontal roof; He has a separated left post.
teachingBeat: Ari draws the bridge and asks learners to count both connected legs.

analogies: a curled handle inside a rounded cup
a round bowl with one rim curled inward
a curled-up garden hose making a cup
pick: cereal bowl, open at the top, with its left rim curling in like a wave
why: Tet is OPEN at the top: a round bowl whose left side rises and curls inward, right side stands straight. Samekh is a sealed ring (no opening); Mem has a pointed/angular roof and its gap is at the bottom-left, not the top. Test: 'Can you drop a spoon in from above?' Only Tet says yes.
teachingBeat: Noa drops a spoon straight into the open top, then traces the little wave curling in on the left.

analogies: a tiny floating comma
a little apostrophe in the air
a small paint droplet with a stubby head
pick: tiny floating comma
why: It floats above the baseline; Vav and Zayin extend much farther downward.
teachingBeat: Rimon bounces beside the tiny floating mark without touching it.

analogies: a rounded open-left mitten
a soft C-shaped bend
a round bowl turned sideways
pick: rounded open-left mitten
why: Its upper-left turn is smooth, unlike Bet’s boxy square roof and floor.
teachingBeat: Ari rounds his hand to follow the curve.

analogies: a tall cane ending in a straight drop
a long-necked hook
a curved roof with an extra-long straight leg
pick: long-necked hook with a straight drop
why: A rounded shoulder and long descending leg; final Nun lacks that broad hooked shoulder.
teachingBeat: Noa traces the curve then runs down its long leg.

analogies: a tall flagpole with a bent flag top
a giraffe neck sticking over the fence
a tall fishing rod with a bent top
pick: flagpole sticking high above the fence
why: Only this common letter rises conspicuously above the normal letter height.
teachingBeat: Ari points up: “This one reaches higher!”

analogies: a folded camping tent with an open bottom-left seam
a zigzag mountain with a closing wall
a little folded map with a gap at the lower left
pick: square lunchbox with one corner popped open (bottom-left)
why: Deliberately paired with the locked Final Mem (sealed lunchbox): same boxy body with a bumpy angular lid, but one corner at the lower-left didn't latch. Final Mem is shut all the way round; Samekh is round with no corners and no gap; Tet is a round bowl open at the TOP, not at a bottom corner. The pair teaches itself: open = Mem, shut = Final Mem.
teachingBeat: Ari wiggles a finger through the popped-open bottom-left corner; Noa then shows Final Mem and clicks it shut.

analogies: a sealed square lunchbox
a closed storage box
a square picture frame with no opening
pick: sealed square lunchbox
why: Four squared connected sides, not Samekh’s rounded loop or Mem’s open seam.
teachingBeat: Ari clicks the square lunchbox shut.

analogies: a little seat with a back on the right
a tiny bent hockey stick
a short L-shaped boot
pick: small right-backed seat
why: Short bent shape with a foot; Vav and final Nun are long straight stems.
teachingBeat: Noa points to the little seat at the baseline.

analogies: an extra-long straight icicle
a long pole sinking below the floor
a thin hanging cord with a top cap
pick: long icicle below the floor
why: Much longer descender than Vav or Zayin, without a base foot.
teachingBeat: Ari draws the floor, then shows the icicle reaching below it.

analogies: a closed round life ring
a round bagel outline
a closed oval race track
pick: closed round life ring
why: Smoothly curved closed loop unlike square final Mem or open folded Mem.
teachingBeat: Rimon peeks through the round hole.

analogies: a two-branch slingshot with one bent arm
a forked tree trunk with a curling branch
two streams joining into one curved river
pick: a lowercase y that sits on the floor: two arms from one low join, tail bent flat, right arm taller
why: Both arms grow from ONE spot down near the floor and nothing continues above or below that join (the tail just bends flat along the baseline). Tsadi's branch joins a stick partway up and the stick keeps going above the join; Aleph's two arms hang off a long diagonal spine. The old slingshot hook was misleading: a slingshot has a handle below the fork, which is actually the Final Tsadi shape.
teachingBeat: Ari puts one finger on the single spot at the floor where both arms start, then runs up the taller right arm.

analogies: a rounded mouth with one tooth inside
a big rounded cup holding one square tooth
a soft sideways pocket with a little tab inside
pick: rounded mouth with one tooth
why: Its clearly visible internal tooth separates Pe from Kaf; curved wall separates it from Bet.
teachingBeat: Ari points to the single tooth inside the mouth.

analogies: a long dangling scarf with a curled top
a tall hanging hook with a little inner tooth
a long-necked mouth open at the top
pick: long hanging hook with an inner tooth
why: Distinctive inner curl/tooth and long downward tail; final Kaf has no inner tooth.
teachingBeat: Noa points to the tiny curl at the top before following the long tail.

analogies: two branches joined like a tilted cactus
a bent twig with a second branch crossing it
a diagonal twig attached to a standing branch
pick: hockey stick standing on its blade, with a little branch leaning on the shaft halfway up
why: Right-hand shaft bends at the bottom into a blade running left along the floor; a diagonal branch from the upper-left joins the shaft PARTWAY UP, and the shaft continues above the join. Ayin's two arms meet at the bottom with nothing above the join; Aleph has no blade on the floor and its spine is diagonal. Pairs with Final Tsadi (same stick, blade gone).
teachingBeat: Ari taps the blade on the floor, then the spot halfway up the shaft where the branch leans in.

analogies: a long stick with a diagonal twig
a tree branch with one very long trunk
a diagonal ski pole alongside a longer vertical pole
pick: the same hockey stick with no blade: the shaft drops straight through the floor, branch still leaning on it
why: Same leaning branch as Tsadi, but no foot along the baseline; the shaft plunges below the floor. Final Nun is a bare icicle with no branch; Final Kaf has a rounded hooked shoulder and no branch; regular Tsadi keeps its blade and stays on the floor. Test: 'branch + goes below the floor' = Final Tsadi.
teachingBeat: Noa draws the floor line, shows the shaft poking through it, then points to the branch that is still leaning on.

analogies: a table with one leg dropping through the floor
a roof over a dangling cord
a little counter with one extra-long leg
pick: table with a leg below the floor
why: One descending post extends below baseline and is detached from the roof, unlike He.
teachingBeat: Ari shows the table leg poking below the floor line.

analogies: a rounded umbrella handle corner
a soft bent pipe
a rounded upside-down L
pick: rounded bent pipe
why: Curved shoulder has no sharp Dalet corner or protruding straight roof.
teachingBeat: Noa draws a round turn with her finger, not a square corner.

analogies: three candle flames on one holder
a three-pronged garden fork
three mountain peaks sharing one base
pick: three candle flames on one holder
why: Three upward branches joining at bottom; no other letter has this clear triple crown.
teachingBeat: Ari counts the three flame tips with Rimon.

analogies: a roof with a left boot and a right leg
a sturdy gate with a bent left foot
a rectangular doorway with a curled left foot
pick: gate with a bent left boot
why: Connected top plus distinct bent left foot separates Tav from Chet’s straight two legs.
teachingBeat: Noa taps the bent boot at the left foot of the gate.
